title: NetworkView
description: One level of the one network (#763, agents/research/redesign/NETWORK.md §4): what a projector computes from a scope's documents and every canvas draws – the creator's Flow tab, the native deck editor, the Reception tab, the MCP. The documents stay the truth; a view is never stored (only its canvas). Each scope's projector lives where that scope's rules live (story: shared/content; XR: the OSCT logic package; show and rig: the Rust core). Edit this file, run `npm run generate` (server/schema/generate.ts writes the Rust and TS types), commit the outputs; network-view.vectors.json holds the views every language reads.

Signal.description: What travels on a port or edge – deck-kit's one signal table (deck/kit/src/base/signal.rs, owner 2026-11-17 [design]): its shapes and colours draw every port and wire. OSCT's `value` is `control`, its `node` is `address`, its `media` is `picture`.

Scope.description: Which documents a view projects: `story` chapters and toons, `xr` experiences, `show` rows and cells, `rig` rigs and instruments, `scene` deck scenes, `creator` the creator's own events (generation done, approved, published …), `network` the levels above them all.

Runtime.description: Where a node runs: the `reader` (the VN runner), `xr` (OSCT's engine in the reader), the `conductor`, a `deck` (the engine, its own audio context), the `server` (jobs, generations), the `editor` (authoring-time nodes only, never at reading time).

Family.description: A node's family – how a canvas draws it and what a gesture may do. `container` can be entered (a chapter, a group, a row, a cell, a track); `world` comes from outside the level with an image of its origin (MIDI, clock, carrier bag, VN state); `free` lives only in the canvas (a reference, a generation, a manual instruction – OSCT L11–L13); `far` is a stub's far end.

Transport.description: How an edge crosses runtimes: `same` (one runtime), `relay` (the Live relay), `navigation` (the reader moves to another place), `savegame` (a variable or item read elsewhere).

Level.description: One step of the breadcrumb, root first.

address.description: The level's address in the one grammar (rig/address.rs), e.g. `chapter:sandbox/1/2`.

many.description: Several edges may meet here (a multi-in socket).

hidden.description: Unused and folded behind the node's `+`.

kind.description: The registered node type (a scope's projector or a module names it).

address.description: What the node is, in the one grammar.

enter.description: The address of the level a double-click opens; none: a leaf.

picture.description: An asset reference for the node's image (a world node's origin, a preview).

group.description: The canvas group it sits in.

Home.description: The one document field that holds an edge or a node: an edit is an op on it. None on an edge: derived (a by-name join, a computed link).

path.description: A JSON pointer into the document.

count.description: A bundle of this many edges of one kind between one pair.

Stub.description: An edge that leaves the level, named by its far end; following it changes the view's scope.

edge.description: The edge's id; its node at the level's edge is a `far` node.

at.description: A node's or an edge's id.

Canvas.description: Authoring data beside the documents, never played: groups, notes, folds, positions pinned by hand (rem) over the auto layout.
